az_welcome_wall.blurb: This limestone sport wall sits in the Homestead canyon of Gila County, central Arizona. It is the gentlest wall in the canyon, so it works well as a warm-up stop or for newer leaders. All eight lines are bolted single pitches: one at 5.7, two at 5.8, and five around 5.10. The face picks up morning sun, which makes it a pleasant early start. The short walk in follows a bouldery wash, so wear shoes with decent grip for loose cobbles.
az_welcome_wall.approach: Drop into the wash and follow the creek bed upstream for roughly a quarter mile; the first large wall on your left is this one.

az_east_face_3.blurb: A tall, steep wall on the east side of Baboquivari Peak in southern Arizona, finishing just below the true summit. It holds long, committing multi-pitch lines, mostly traditional, plus one aid route and one alpine-style route, spanning easy fifth-class terrain up into the 5.11 range. Most routes begin from a brushy shelf that crosses the face. Rock quality is mixed. This is a serious backcountry objective rather than a casual crag, and a long approach comes before any climbing.
az_east_face_3.approach: Follow the trail up to the saddle, continue along to the brushy ledge system, then scramble through vegetation and ledges to the base of the main routes.
